fix_applied.summary: DynamoDB moved out of LocalStack into a standalone amazon/dynamodb-local container (infra/docker-compose.yml), reachable at a separate AWS_ENDPOINT_URL-style property (AwsProperties#dynamoDbEndpointUrl) than SNS/SQS (which stay on LocalStack). Root cause and diagnostic ladder: docs/load/BOTTLENECK.md.
fix_applied.root_cause: LocalStack's own DynamoDB support proxies every call through an internal Python HTTP client (a plain requests.Session, via rolo's SimpleRequestsClient) to the same DynamoDBLocal.jar this fix runs directly -- but that internal proxy has a fixed, non-configurable connection-pool cap (requests' library default, pool_maxsize=10) that became the throughput ceiling under load.
fix_applied.raw_throughput_before_after: ~45 ops/s (LocalStack-proxied, file-backed heap=256MB) -> ~400 ops/s (LocalStack-proxied, in-memory heap=1g) -> ~800-950 ops/s (standalone dynamodb-local, no proxy) -- three separate confirmed measurements, each a distinct fix layered on the last.
fix_applied.app_throughput_before_after: ~8.5-8.9 req/s -> ~158-201 req/s (S2, this document) -- roughly a 19x improvement, comfortably clearing the >=100 req/s target.

trimming_rule.rationale: Unchanged from the original pass: docs/load/artifacts/s2-dry-run-*.ndjson showed a clean bimodal split before any load test ran. 10000ms sits in the empty gap between the two populations.
trimming_rule.status_after_fix: The trim rule stays valid across every stage tested in this pass (removed_rate stayed in a 0-4% band throughout S0/S1/S2/S3 -- no stage showed the >50% breakdown seen pre-fix at S2 vus=100/200, because trimmed latencies now stay far below the 10s threshold even at the highest stage tested).

environment_limitation.summary: The WSL2 clock-jump artifact (docs/load/BOTTLENECK.md RUNG 4: real, periodic multi-second stalls inside whichever DynamoDB-serving process is under load, not a measurement artifact) is still present post-fix, at a lower rate: S0's stall rate dropped from 4.21% to 1.02% at the same 1 VU / ~1 req/s baseline. The artifact is orthogonal to the throughput fix -- both are real, independently confirmed, and this pass does not re-litigate RUNG 4's finding.
environment_limitation.portability: Unchanged: the shape of the capacity behavior (a flat throughput ceiling, Little's-Law-consistent queueing beneath it) is portable; the absolute ~160-200 req/s number is specific to this dynamodb-local container on this machine.

caveats: dynamodb-local (the standalone container) is still a single-process DynamoDB Local instance, not real AWS DynamoDB -- its latency/throughput characteristics under concurrent transactional load do not represent production DynamoDB, even after removing LocalStack's proxy layer.

Only 2 of the 208 seeded accounts (alice/acc-001, bob/acc-002) are "real" fixtures reused from earlier steps; the other 206 are load-test-only ring/exhaustible accounts created by tools/k6/seed/seed-load-test-fixtures.sh.
fraud-service has no runtime latency/failure-injection knob -- s4_fraud below did not run; see docs/steps/step-64.md (proposed, unimplemented).

No HTTP connection-pool or thread-pool tuning was found in any service's application.yml -- Tomcat runs its Spring Boot default (max-threads=200); not implicated in this pass (S2 never showed a genuine capacity error up to 150 VUs).
This is WSL2 on Windows (Docker Desktop backend), not bare-metal Linux.

S2's fraud_denied_rate is NOT monotonic in VUs and is NOT a capacity signal -- see the s2_capacity section below and docs/load/RESULTS.md for the mechanism (ring-account concentration at low VU counts crosses fraud-service's velocity threshold faster than at high VU counts, which spread load across more distinct accounts).
